# rocelet resources and timing

*Generated by `synth/report.py` from `make synth` and `make synth-variants` (Vivado 2025.2, 2026-11-05).*

Out-of-context results on **xcku5p-ffvb676-2-e** (the KCU116 device) with the clock at the 100G CMAC user clock, **322.265625 MHz (3.103 ns)**, unless noted. Out of context means no I/O buffers and no optimisation across the IP boundary; in a full design the numbers are usually slightly lower. BRAM36 counts RAMB36 tiles plus half a tile per RAMB18. WNS / WHS: worst setup / hold slack, positive = met.

## v1 configuration (v0.3.0)

The parameter defaults of `rocelet_top`: 16 QPs, 16 memory windows, READ depth 16, a 256 KB URAM retransmit ring (`RTX_MODE` "RING"), 128 outstanding work requests, RX ICRC check, shared CRC network, HSB builder mode, VLAN, PAUSE, ARP/ICMP, other-traffic ports, counters, 32 KB RX and TX FIFOs, 16 KB other-traffic TX FIFO, AXI4 memory master with a 16 KB read buffer.

| | LUT | FF | BRAM36 | URAM | DSP | WNS / WHS (ns) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| synthesis | 21,012 | 25,029 | 37 | 8 | 1 | 0.214 / 0.010 |
| **placed and routed** | **20,732** | **25,122** | **37** | **8** | 1 | **0.105 / 0.035** |
| share of the KU5P | 9.6 % | 5.8 % | 7.7 % | 12.5 % | 0.1 % | |

Worst routed setup path: 0.105 ns, `eng_rst_reg/C` -> `u_mac/u_rxf/ob_rp_reg[0]_rep__1/R`, 0 logic levels.

## MAC widths (v0.3.0)

*Generated by `synth/report.py --mac` from `make synth-mac` (Vivado 2025.2, 2026-11-05).*

The v1 configuration (all other parameters at their defaults) with the MAC AXI-Stream at each `MAC_WIDTH`, placed and routed out of context: 512 bits on the KCU116 device at the 100G CMAC clock (the regression figure against v0.2.2), 256 and 64 bits on the ZCU106 device (**xczu7ev-ffvc1156-2-e**) at the 156.25 MHz clock of a 40G / 10G MAC, with the width converters inside `rocelet_top`. The v0.2.2 row is the routed v1 top of rocelet v0.2.2 (same part and clock), for comparison. The 512-bit build sets `CLK_KHZ` to the exact CMAC clock (322,266 kHz) and is placed and routed in its own run, so it differs slightly from the v1 top above.

| Configuration | Device | LUT | FF | BRAM36 | URAM | DSP | WNS / WHS (ns) | LUT vs v0.2.2 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| v0.2.2 v1 top (512-bit CMAC), 322.27 MHz | KU5P (KCU116) | 20,812 | 25,064 | 37 | 8 | 0 | 0.087 / 0.024 | |
| **v0.3.0 512-bit MAC (100G CMAC), 322.27 MHz** | KU5P (KCU116) | **20,654** | 25,119 | 37 | 8 | 1 | **0.115 / 0.007** | -158 |
| **v0.3.0 256-bit MAC (40GBASE-R4), 156.25 MHz** | ZU7EV (ZCU106) | **20,786** | 26,173 | 37 | 8 | 1 | **1.267 / 0.008** | -26 |
| **v0.3.0 64-bit MAC (10GBASE-R), 156.25 MHz** | ZU7EV (ZCU106) | **21,336** | 26,190 | 37 | 8 | 1 | **1.407 / 0.018** | +524 |

On the ZU7EV the 256-bit build is 9.0 % of the LUTs, 11.9 % of the BRAM36 and 8.3 % of the URAM.

Width converters (routed): 256-bit MAC (40GBASE-R4): RX packer 50 LUT / 581 FF, TX unpacker 152 LUT / 581 FF; 64-bit MAC (10GBASE-R): RX packer 239 LUT / 583 FF, TX unpacker 522 LUT / 587 FF.

The one DSP slice is the received-PAUSE quanta multiply (`PAUSE_QCLK`, since v0.3.0). Reproduce with `make synth-mac` (one Vivado process, the three jobs of `synth/jobs_mac.txt`; reports in `synth/build_mac/`).

## Against AMD's ERNIC IP

| Design | LUT | BRAM36 | URAM | Scope |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **rocelet v0.3.0 `rocelet_top`** (routed, OOC) | **20,732** | **37** | **8** | engine + MAC glue + ARP/ICMP + register file + counters + AXI4 memory master |
| rocelet v0.3.0 `rocelet_core` (synthesis, OOC) | 14,994 | 7 | 8 | engine only |
| AMD ERNIC v4.3, 8 QP (synthesis, OOC) | 42,082 | 117 | 20 | engine only |

`rocelet_core` is 36 % of the ERNIC engine's LUTs (about a third); the whole `rocelet_top` (engine, MAC glue, ARP/ICMP, register file, counters and AXI4 memory master) is 49 % (about half).

## Reproducing

```
make synth            # lint, v1 top (place and route), v1 core
make synth-variants   # the build options
python3 synth/report.py --version rtl   # this page, right after the runs above
make synth-mac        # the MAC widths (also rewrites that section: report.py --mac)
```

`synth/run_synth.sh` waits while two or more Vivado processes run on the machine (`MAX_JOBS`). Reports: `synth/build/<job>_{synth,route}_{util,hier,timing}.rpt` (`synth/build_mac/` for the MAC widths). The Vivado linter (`synth_design -lint`, job `v1_lint`) reports no errors on the v1 top; its warnings are unused ports and signals of disabled options and width notes.
